carbon_policy_signal.item: EU conservatives (EPP) target carbon price on heating and driving, methane rules weakening; ETS scope expansion under political pressure.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Weakening EUA floor reduces fuel-switching incentive from coal to gas in power merit order; direct hit to thermal dispatch economics and gas demand at margin.

freshness_caveat: Coal data stale as of 2025-12-26 (300 days old); 8th-percentile reading cannot be used to validate current dark-spread relative value without refresh. All other metrics current as of 2026-10-20 to 2026-10-22.
risk_flags: Coal data 300 days stale (as of 2025-12-26); 8th-percentile reading may not reflect current cost basis for dark spread valuation.
Storage 14.7pp below seasonal average; refill pace failure into winter could push TTF materially higher if LNG flow disrupted.
EU political fracture on climate (AfD/National Rally sanctions talk, EPP ambivalence on ETS) creates policy tail-risk to EUA floor and forward curve certainty.
UK emergency gas imports from Continent signal latent winter stress; sustained Continental outflows could trigger spot TTF spike if LNG supply tightens.

base.summary: TTF holds 81st-percentile on sanctions certainty, UK imports steady, storage refill modest; EUA stable mid-range; no shocks.

downside.summary: EU political fracture on sanctions escalates (coalition talks signal Russian gas re-entry); carbon reform weakens ETS floor; thermal merit order collapses.

upside.summary: Winter weather tightens (early cold snap); LNG delays or supply disruption (refinery outage, shipping); storage refill stalls below 60%. TTF spikes.

themes: Sanctions regime locks EU into LNG dependency; political fracture on climate/ETS weighs on carbon floor
Storage deficit + UK emergency imports tighten NW European gas balance heading into winter
Coal historically cheap but data stale; dark spread asymmetric upside on TTF strength
Conservative push to weaken ETS scope and carbon pricing reduces fuel-switch incentive
top_drivers: Sanctions hold + UK emergency imports reinforce NW European gas tightness; TTF at 81st-percentile reflects winter LNG dependency.
Storage 14.7pp below seasonal average creates structural call on imported gas; refill pace into Nov–Dec will set Q4-Q1 power curve.
Conservative political pressure on ETS (EPP, AfD, National Rally) threatens carbon-floor enforcement; weakens fuel-switch incentive and could depress TTF upside if carbon collapses.
Coal at 8th-percentile nominally attractive vs gas, but 300-day staleness means dark-spread relative value unconfirmed; fresh data essential before sizing thermal hedge.
top_takeaway: TTF at 81st-percentile (+19% M/M) backstopped by sanctions hold and UK emergency imports; coal at 8th-percentile (stale) creates massive dark-spread skew; storage 14.7pp below seasonal average supports winter premium.

watchlist.why: EPP dominance may delay or weaken carbon cap enforcement, pressuring EUA forward and reducing gas-vs-coal switching incentive.

watchlist.metric: UK-EU gas pipeline capacity deal terms
watchlist.why: Emergency import commitment signals winter supply anxiety; sustained reverse flows could strain TTF if LNG import pace falters.

watchlist.metric: Winter gas supply stress test (LNG, storage refill path)
watchlist.why: At 74.58% full and 14.7pp below seasonal, storage buffer relies on continuous LNG inflow; any supply disruption or weather cold-spell will drive TTF materially higher.

watchlist.metric: AfD/National Rally coalition talks on Russia sanctions
watchlist.why: Political pressure to resume cheap Russian gas creates medium-term tail-risk to sanctions integrity; any signal of relief would crater TTF and undermine EU LNG negotiating leverage.
Current data (300 days old) is stale; fresh read critical to validate dark-spread opportunity sizing and coal-gas merit-order assumptions for winter.

watchlist_dated.name: EU Council climate vote (if scheduled this week)
watchlist_dated.why: ETS scope revision outcome feeds directly into EUA floor and gas switch economics.
